title: What Does a Bias Head Measure? Non-Identifiability in Head-Level Bias Attribution
abstract: arXiv:2611.23218v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Methods that localise social bias in large language models to individual attention heads and remove it by ablation are validated by their effect on a fairness metric, never by evidence that the statistic selecting the heads measures bias. We audit this on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The head map correlates at $\rho = -0.950$ and $-0.768$ with a label-blind response-length map, apparently identifying a surface confound. An intervention that breaks the length-label coupling rejects this reading: with the prompt held fixed, response length explains 1% of the statistic's variance. What does explain it is prompt identity, at 64% of variance, in an ordering that is not monotonic in length. Within any fixed prompt the fairness label, response length and the presence of a protected-group token are collinear at $\phi = 0.95$, partly by definition of the labelling rule, so no observational analysis can attribute the map to any

translated_title: 偏差注意力头究竟测量了什么？头级偏差归因中的不可辨识性
translated_abstract: 目前将大语言模型中的社会偏差定位到单个注意力头并通过消融（ablation）来消除偏差的方法，通常仅通过其对公平性指标的影响来验证，而从未验证过用于选择注意力头的统计量是否真正测量了偏差。我们在 Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct 和 Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 上对这一方法进行了审计。该头级图谱与一个不依赖标签的响应长度图谱相关系数分别达到 ρ = -0.950 和 -0.768，表面上似乎识别出一个混淆因素。然而，一项打破长度与标签耦合关系的干预实验否定了这一解读：在提示保持固定的情况下，响应长度仅能解释该统计量方差的 1%。真正能解释该统计量的是提示本身的身份，占方差的 64%，且其排序与长度并不呈单调关系。在任何固定的提示内，公平性标签、响应长度与受保护群体标记的出现三者之间的共线性高达 φ = 0.95，这部分源于标注规则的定义本身，因此任何观察性分析都无法将该图谱归因于任何单一因素（摘要原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文审计了将LLM偏差归因于单个注意力头的常用方法，发现用于选头的统计量主要由提示身份驱动（占64%方差），而公平性标签、响应长度与受保护群体标记之间存在固有共线性，证明头级偏差归因本质上是不可辨识的。
en_tdlr: The paper audits head-level bias attribution in LLMs and shows that the head-selecting statistic is driven mainly by prompt identity (64% of variance) rather than response length, while fairness labels, response length, and protected-group tokens are inherently collinear, making head-level bias attribution fundamentally non-identifiable.
